hero.alt: A person holding a small lantern on a foggy country path, the next few steps lit.

hardDay.heading: Hard day? Start here.
hardDay.body:
If you're clarity-hungry, you're probably not lazy. You're sincere. Maybe you've seen foolish leaps called faith. Maybe certainty once felt like survival. Begin with honesty and one inch.

When Peter began to sink, Jesus took hold of him. Read "A Pastoral Word to the Clarity-Hungry."

If you are in danger, or you are having thoughts of not wanting to live, please stop here and reach out now. In the U.S., call or text 988, or call 911. Then tell a pastor or a trusted believer today.

bookRef.section: A Pastoral Word to the Clarity-Hungry

read.heading: Read first: Chapter 9
read.body:
Open to Chapter 9, "Action in the Fog." Read "Fog Is Weather, Not Always a Verdict" and "Concrete Practices for Foggy Days."

The first section is for anyone who's treated uncertainty as a stop sign. A lamp lights the next few steps, not the whole road. And if you're the kind of person with forty tabs open on one decision, there's a line in there for you.

The second section is the practical one: pray specifically, open the Word, sort what's clear from what isn't, and take one step soon. Read it, then come back.

bookRef.section: Fog Is Weather, Not Always a Verdict; Concrete Practices for Foggy Days

read.quote: More browser windows are not the same as more light.
prompts: What fog am I treating as a permanent stop sign?

pulse.heading: The pulse: enough light for the next step
pulse.body:
Faith moves with enough light for the next step, not full visibility.

Scripture walks into fog with us. Abraham went not knowing where. Israel followed a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night. Peter stepped out of the boat. Sheep hear and follow, and following means motion.

bookRef.section: Scripture Walks Into Fog With Us

verses.text: for we walk by faith, not by sight.

And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them along the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, that they might travel by day and by night. The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not depart from before the people.

prompts: Am I asking for wisdom, or demanding stadium lights before I move?

nameIt.heading: Name it: waiting or pause?
nameIt.body:
Holy waiting keeps today's faithfulness. A permanent pause uses every unanswered question as a reason to do nothing, and it slowly becomes a prison.

Ask the waiting question honestly. While you wait on the big thing, are you still doing today's small things?

verses.text: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make straight your paths.

prompts: What fog am I treating as a permanent stop sign, when I already have lamp-light for the next inch?
While I wait, am I keeping today's faithfulness?
Which clear duty have I been postponing?

build.heading: Build it: clear and unclear
build.body:
Fog gets smaller when you pull apart what's clear and what isn't. Usually there's more in the clear pile than fear wants you to see.

Make two lists. In the first: what Scripture already says, what's already your job today, and what wise people in your life have confirmed. In the second: what you still don't know.

Pick one faithful inch from the first list. Hold the rest loosely. If God shuts a door, accept it. If one opens, test it with the Word and wise counsel, then go.

move.heading: Move: this week's practice
move.body:
From the end of Chapter 9:

Take one faithful inch in the fog within 24 to 72 hours: an email, an appointment, a conversation, a small obedience. Review afterward. Did I obey? What did I learn?

Not the whole journey. One inch. If the window closes, set a new one within three days.

Did I obey?
What did I learn?
Missed it? New time (within three days):
move.cta: Close the app and go take your step

help.heading: Help: walk in the fog together
help.body:
Bring one answer to a trusted believer this week. Show them your clear and unclear lists and ask what they see.

Then think of someone stuck in their own fog. Don't hand them a five-year plan. Offer to help them write their own two lists, or just sit with them while they send the one email.

help.cta: Send it, then put the phone down

pray.heading: Pray it: wisdom for the next step
pray.body:
Chapter 9 says to pray specifically. Not "show me everything." Ask for the next faithful step.

Father, I don't see mile twenty. Give me wisdom for the next step in ____.

I'm Your sheep. Help me hear Your voice in Your Word and follow. I surrender the outcome. Give me a teachable heart, not just a clear schedule.

I'll take this inch by ____. Amen.

verses.text: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.

prompts: The decision I'm naming:

review.heading: Review: fog-faith revisits and continues
review.body:
After your inch, mark it: took the step, not yet, or holy wait.

Guardrail from Chapter 9: fog-faith isn't presumption. It isn't demanding a map. And it never means ignoring red flags or wise counsel.

When Peter began to sink, Jesus reached out and caught him. Fog doesn't empty your hands of today's assignment. That's where we go next.

bookRef.section: Guardrails: What Fog-Faith Is Not; Toward What Is Already in Your Hand

verses.text: And Peter answered him, “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the water.” He said, “Come.” So Peter got out of the boat and walked on the water and came to Jesus. But when he saw the wind, he was afraid, and beginning to sink he cried out, “Lord, save me.” Jesus immediately reached out his hand and took hold of him, saying to him, “O you of little faith, why did you doubt?”
